# DG Create Engineering Ticket

Create an Engineering ticket that another engineer can understand and implement without rediscovering its intent or scope.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. It is in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

## Canonical template

The canonical Linear template is [General Engineering Task](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/new?template=6ca39698-3bce-449a-992e-059f0334e15b). Keep this link only as a reference in this skill. Never add it to a created ticket.

Use this exact template as the drafting checklist:

```markdown
## Problem

- What accepted user, developer, or project need does this address?
- Why does it need to be solved now?

## Solution

- What is the smallest change that solves the problem?

## Done When

- Describe how success is verified (behavioral or technical).
- Remember: Make only the smallest change needed to solve the problem.
- Remember: **Stay within the defined scope, or communicate any scope increase**

## Out of Scope

- (Optional) What adjacent cases, abstractions, or future work are explicitly not included?
- Link follow-up tickets where applicable

## Notes

- Additional Context, Blockers, dependencies, or follow-up actions.
```

Every bullet above is placeholder guidance. Replace or remove every placeholder before presenting a draft or creating a ticket. Keep all five headings, leaving `Out of Scope` or `Notes` empty when nothing useful applies. Use 1–3 short bullets per section unless the ticket is genuinely complex.

## Agent provenance and human review

Always use the Engineering team. This skill never creates or redirects to Feedback.

- Create every agent-created ticket in the existing `Ticket Draft` status with exactly one existing workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group. The label records provenance and stays after approval.
- Select the label from the creating agent's known identity: `Created by Claude` for Claude, `Created by Codex` for Codex, or `Created by LLM` for any other agent or when its identity cannot be determined. Do not infer agent identity from the Linear account, ticket topic, or skill name. Do not use `Created by LLM` as a substitute when the correct agent-specific label is missing.
- `Ticket Draft` is in the Backlog category and means human ticket review is pending; it does not authorize implementation. The existing `Draft` status belongs to the Started category and is used by the PR workflow. Do not use it for ticket review or change its automation.
- In `Notes`, record `Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket` and any other creation skills actually used. Skill attribution is provenance, not evidence that the ticket meets the standards.
- The human who asked the agent to create the ticket checks intent against the source request, scope and exclusions, verifiable acceptance criteria, and the canonical template and engineering writing standards. Keep the ticket in `Ticket Draft` while changes are needed.
- Human approval moves the ticket to `Backlog` when the problem and fix are agreed and implementation needs no further product or solution decisions. Use `Triage` when implementation is likely within six months but decisions remain. Keep idea-stage Engineering requests in Engineering.
- The human's move from `Ticket Draft` to `Triage` or `Backlog` records sign-off. An agent may make that move only after explicit human approval of the completed ticket and destination. A request to create a ticket is not approval of its generated contents. Keep the provenance label and skill attribution.

## Project selection

Every ticket must use an existing project that is not completed, canceled, archived, or trashed. Resolve the project in this order:

1. Use the project explicitly named by the user.
2. Use a clearly relevant active project from the current work context.
3. For Roam work, use `Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks`.
4. For Obsidian work, use `Obsidian Discourse Graphs plugin assorted tasks`.
5. Otherwise, use `Engineering Ops assorted tasks`.

Confirm the selected project still exists, is active, and includes the Engineering team. Never create a project. If a user-specified project is missing, ambiguous, or inactive, ask the user for another project instead of silently substituting one.

## Labels and optional fields

- Inspect existing issue labels and apply every clearly relevant label.
- Never create a label or guess an uncertain label.
- Missing or uncertain optional labels do not block creation. If `Ticket Draft` or the required provenance label is missing or ambiguous, return the prepared draft and report the configuration gap instead of creating an unmarked ticket or substituting a status.
- Set priority only when the user or context makes it clear and useful.
- Do not set a cycle or release. CI/CD handles releases.

## Create or draft

Draft without changing Linear when the user asks for a draft, review, or rewrite. Create the ticket without an additional confirmation when the user explicitly asks to create it.

Before creation, resolve the current Engineering statuses, selected project, and existing labels. Create the issue once with its title, completed description (including skill attribution), `Ticket Draft` status, project, provenance and relevant labels, and justified priority. If the result is ambiguous, search for the issue before retrying so a transient failure does not create a duplicate.

Read the created issue back and verify its status, labels, and attribution. Report any mismatch instead of claiming successful routing. Return the issue identifier, title, status, project, and link, and say that human review is pending. Include the generated branch name when Linear returns one. Do not restate the full description unless the user asks.

## Creating a new canvas

### Using the command palette

1. Open the command palette (`Cmd/Ctrl + P`)
2. Search for "Create new Discourse Graph canvas"
3. Press Enter to create a new canvas

![Create canvas command](/docs/obsidian/create-canvas-command.png)
The canvas will be created in your configured canvas folder (default: the vault root) with a timestamp-based filename like `Canvas-2025-01-15-1430.md`.

1. Open the file of the canvas

![Canvas icon button](/docs/obsidian/canvas-icon-button.png)

  safe to edit. See [Avoiding data loss](#avoiding-data-loss).
</Callout>

1. Click the **Discourse Graph** icon in the bottom toolbar
2. In the panel on the right, click a node type to select it (or drag a node type onto the canvas)
3. Click on the canvas where you want the node
4. In the **Create discourse node** modal, enter a title, confirm the node type, and click **Confirm**
   The new node appears on the canvas as a discourse node card linked to the note that was created.

![Create discourse node](/docs/obsidian/create-discourse-node.gif)

![drag-node](/docs/obsidian/file-explorer-drag.gif)

1. In a note, find a wikilink or markdown link to a discourse node (for example `[[CLM - My claim]]`)
2. Drag using the handle next to the link
3. Drop onto the canvas

The handle appears for `[[wikilinks]]` and `[markdown links](path.md)` that point to notes in your vault. It does not appear on image embeds (`![[...]]`).

![drag-node](/docs/obsidian/editor-drag-node.gif)

Turn tldraw text or image shapes into discourse nodes without leaving the canvas:

1. Select a **text** or **image** shape on the canvas
2. Right-click the shape

4. In the modal, edit the title (text is pre-filled; images start with an empty title) or search for an existing node

2. Open the discourse context by clicking the telescope icon on the left bar

## Understanding relationship types

Relationship types define how different nodes in your discourse graph can connect to each other. Each relationship type has:

- A primary label (e.g., "supports")
- A complement label (e.g., "is supported by")
- Rules about which node types can be connected

## Adding relationship types

1. Open Obsidian Settings
2. Navigate to the "Discourse Graphs" settings tab
3. Under "Relation Types," click "Add Relationship Type"
4. Configure the relationship:
   - Enter the primary label (e.g., "supports", "contradicts")
   - Enter the complement label (e.g., "is supported by", "is contradicted by")
     ![add relation type](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2Fjk367dcO_K.png?alt=media&token=22d74e9f-882c-434b-8b50-afd7a754fb2b)
5. Click "Save Changes"

## Configuring valid relationships

After creating relationship types, you need to define which node types can be connected by each relationship.

1. Open the Discourse Relations tab in settings
   ![discourse relation](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FNgm7Ha4Ul5.png?alt=media&token=a933bd3a-d9a6-42c1-9c6e-d779d41c7ebf)

2. Choose the components:
   - Source Node Type (e.g., Claim)
   - Relationship Type (e.g., supports)
   - Target Node Type (e.g., Question)
     ![choose relation](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FlflJBkfdaK.png?alt=media&token=5de9617c-6099-46e8-931f-feafc604cabb)

3. Review and confirm the configuration
   ![final relations](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FycPW-N-rY8.png?alt=media&token=54867be2-9030-4c6c-82d2-b96069e52d81)

## Example relationships

Here are some common relationship types:

- Claim → supports → Question
- Evidence → supports → Claim
- Evidence → contradicts → Claim
- Source → informs → Question

## Related

- [Create your first relationship](/docs/obsidian/core-features/creating-discourse-relationships)
- [Learn about the discourse context](/docs/obsidian/core-features/discourse-context)
- [Explore your graph](/docs/obsidian/core-features/canvas)

Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify

# Obsidian CDP verify

## The one command

From the worktree root:

```sh
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs \
  --slot 1 --marker "<string only this change's bundle contains>" \
  --scenario path/to/scenarios.mjs [--scenario more.mjs] [--port 9222] [--skip-build]
```

It runs doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 vault locked, 3 marker missing.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- Slots come from `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env`. It takes a JSON array or a comma list of plugin dirs or vault roots. `--slot N` is 1-based and defaults to 1.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved slot, the lock and the Obsidian state. If another live run holds the lock, it exits 2 and asks you to switch slot. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about competing `dev.ts`/esbuild watchers. Your own worktree's watcher counts too, if it mirrors into the same vault.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |
| `waitFor` on an IIFE always times out | `evaluate` adds an outer `return` only when the code contains no `return`. An IIFE with an inner `return` evaluates to `undefined`, so write `return (() => { ... })()`. |
| A note written in `setup` is randomly missing from search results | Datacore indexes new files after the metadata cache, and the search loads through Datacore. After `writeNote`, also `waitFor` `dc.query("@page and exists(nodeTypeId)")` to include the path. |
